belote.rules: You and North against West and East, 32 cards (7 to ace). Take the turned-up suit as trump or pass; in round two name another suit; if all pass, deal again. Trump: jack 20, nine 14, ace 11, ten 10, king 4, queen 3. Other suits: ace 11, ten 10, king 4, queen 3, jack 2. Follow suit; if you cannot, trump unless your partner is winning, and beat the best trump if you can. King and queen of trump together: belote, 20. Last trick 10. The takers need 82 of 162; if they fall short the others score 162. All eight tricks is capot: 252. First to the target wins. Tap a card to play it, or drag it to the middle.

bigtwo.rules: Four players, 13 cards each. Whoever holds the 3 of diamonds leads a hand that includes it. Each player must play the same kind of hand, higher, or pass; when all others pass the last player leads anything. Hands: single, pair, three of a kind, and five cards: straight, flush, full house, four of a kind plus a card, straight flush (in that order; straights run 3 up to 10 J Q K A). Twos are highest, then aces; suits rank diamonds, clubs, hearts, spades. First out wins the hand and is paid one point a card from each other player (double at 10 or more, triple at 13). First to 30 wins. Tap cards to pick them, then Play. P plays, S passes, H hints.

bridge.rules: Chicago bridge: four deals, you (South) and North against West and East. Bid a contract (level 1 to 7 is tricks past six, in clubs, diamonds, hearts, spades or no trump); three passes after a bid end the auction. Declarer plays both hands, dummy goes down after the opening lead. Follow suit; the highest trump, else the highest card of the suit led, takes the trick. Game (100 trick points) is worth 300, or 500 vulnerable; slams and doubles score more, undertricks cost 50 or 100. The computers bid a natural system: 5-card majors, 15 to 17 NT, Stayman (2 clubs after 1NT). Tap a card to play it; when you are declarer, tap dummy’s cards too. Players can be any of the four seats: with two or more people in the Players rows, each sees only their own hand, behind a handoff.

canasta.rules: Two-handed Canasta against the computer. Draw two cards, or take the discard pile; lay down melds of three or more of a rank; discard one card. Twos and jokers are wild (a meld needs two natural cards, at most three wild, never more wild than natural). Seven cards make a canasta: 500 pure, 300 mixed. Red threes score 100 each and are laid at once; black threes only go out. Your first meld needs 50 points (more as your score rises). The pile is frozen after a wild discard, or before you have melded: take it only with a natural pair matching the top card. Going out needs two canastas (100, or 200 if you laid everything in one turn). Pick cards by tapping them, then Meld, Discard or Take pile (or tap the stock to draw). Keys: D draw, T take, M meld, X discard, Esc clear. First to the goal wins.

skat.rules: Three players, 32 cards, ten each and two in the skat. Bid by the value of the game you promise (18, 20, 22, 23, 24, 27, 30 ...). The declarer takes the skat, puts two cards back and names a game: a suit (jacks and that suit are trump; clubs 12, spades 11, hearts 10, diamonds 9), grand (only the jacks, 24) or null (no tricks wanted, 23). Playing from the hand without the skat scores more. Ace 11, ten 10, king 4, queen 3, jack 2: the declarer needs 61. Value is the base times the matadors (the top jacks in a row, with or without) plus game, hand, schneider and schwarz. A win scores 50 plus the value; a loss costs 50 plus twice the value and the defenders score 30 each. If all pass, the hand is dealt again. Highest total after the series wins. Tap a card to play it, or drag it to the middle.

sky.fact.aldebaran: Aldebaran is the red eye of the bull in Taurus.
sky.fact.altair: Altair spins so fast that it is flattened, turning once in under ten hours.
sky.fact.antares: Antares is a red supergiant, and its name means rival of Mars.
sky.fact.arcturus: Arcturus is an orange giant about 37 light-years away. Follow the handle of the Big Dipper to find it.
sky.fact.betelgeuse: Betelgeuse is a red supergiant so large that it would swallow the orbit of Mars.
sky.fact.canopus: Canopus is the second brightest star, a giant that spacecraft use to find their way.
sky.fact.capella: Capella is really two yellow giants, about 43 light-years away.
sky.fact.deneb: Deneb is one of the most luminous stars we can see, about 2,600 light-years away.
sky.fact.fomalhaut: Fomalhaut is called the loneliest star, because no other bright star is near it.
sky.fact.jupiter: Jupiter is the largest planet. With binoculars you can see its four biggest moons.
sky.fact.mars: Mars looks red because its dust is rich in iron oxide, which is rust.
sky.fact.mercury: Mercury is the smallest planet and stays so close to the Sun that it is only seen near dawn or dusk.
sky.fact.polaris: Polaris hardly moves because it sits almost straight above Earth’s north pole.
sky.fact.procyon: Procyon means before the dog: it rises ahead of Sirius, the Dog Star.
sky.fact.regulus: Regulus is the heart of Leo, the lion.
sky.fact.rigel: Rigel is a blue supergiant more than a hundred thousand times as bright as the Sun.
sky.fact.saturn: Saturn’s rings are ice and rock, and so thin that they all but vanish when seen edge on.
sky.fact.sirius: Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky, only 8.6 light-years away.
sky.fact.spica: Spica is really two stars that circle each other every four days.
sky.fact.vega: Vega was the north pole star about 14,000 years ago and will be again around the year 13,700.
sky.fact.venus: Venus is the brightest planet. It is nearly as big as Earth and wrapped in thick cloud.

tienlen.rules: Four players, 13 cards each. Whoever holds the 3 of spades leads a hand that includes it. Play a single, pair, three or four of a kind, a run of three or more cards in a row, or a run of three or more pairs in a row, matching what is on the table and higher, or pass; a pass keeps you out of that round. Twos are highest (never in a run); suits rank spades, clubs, diamonds, hearts. Chop a two: four of a kind or three pairs in a row beats a single two; four of a kind or four pairs in a row beats a pair of twos. Play goes on until three are out; finishing first to last scores 4, 1, -1, -4. First to 12 wins. Tap cards to pick them, then Play. P plays, S passes, H hints.

tp.rules: Everyone puts in a boot of 10 and gets three cards face down. Play blind (without looking) or look and play seen. The stake starts at 10: a blind player pays the stake (or double to raise it); a seen player pays double (or four times to raise, which doubles the stake). Pack folds. A seen player may ask the seen player before him for a side show: the weaker hand packs (a tie packs the asker). With two players left, Show turns the hands over: the higher wins (a tie goes to the one who did not ask). Hands, best first: trail (three of a kind), pure sequence (straight flush), sequence (straight), colour (flush), pair, high card. A-2-3 is the highest sequence, then A-K-Q down to 4-3-2. Asha plays carefully, Dev boldly and Rani bluffs. If you run short you go all in and the hands are shown. Reach 1500 chips to win, or outlast the others; you lose when you cannot pay the boot.

truco.rules: Three cards each; win two of three tricks. Highest cards: ace of espadas, ace of bastos, 7 of espadas, 7 of oros, then all 3s, 2s, the aces of copas and oros, 12s, 11s, 10s, the other 7s, 6s, 5s, 4s. Tied trick: the first trick tie goes to whoever wins the second; a later tie goes to the first trick’s winner, else to mano. Envido (first trick only): two cards of one suit count 20 plus their values, figures count 0, otherwise your best card; the higher wins (mano on a tie). Envido is worth 2, real envido 3, falta envido the points the leader still needs; a refusal gives the caller what was already on the table, at least 1. Truco: worth 2, retruco 3, vale cuatro 4; a refusal gives the caller the value before the call. Mazo folds the hand. Tap a card to play it.
